scope: Candidate language-native formal interfaces and explicit semantic design review

source_basis.hashes: Each source anchor carries the file SHA256. Source facts are not runtime observations.

runtime_basis.rule: The frozen SDK may differ from current source. Preserve both observations; do not infer one from the other.

status_vocabulary.catalogued: A candidate with a concrete BL job and model boundary.
status_vocabulary.implemented: An executable public specimen is linked; qualification may still be missing.
status_vocabulary.qualified: A retained run establishes this fragment/result/profile on a named artifact.
status_vocabulary.bounded: Exact only within stated finite universe/length/depth.
status_vocabulary.abstract: A deliberately weaker/abstract model; refinement conditions remain.
status_vocabulary.unsupported: The requested operation/result is explicitly refused.
status_vocabulary.unknown: The backend did not decide the stated query.

families.title: Bool and BL truthiness
families.semantic_boundary: Only nil and false are falsey in current BL. The symbolic Bool sort accepts only true/false. Do not coerce arbitrary symbolic values implicitly.

implementation.claim: Implementation must be linked separately; a module or method name is not qualification.

families.title: Unbounded integers
families.semantic_boundary: SMT Int is unbounded; nonlinear integer solving may be incomplete. Resource caps do not change the mathematical domain.

implementation.claim: Implementation must be linked separately; a module or method name is not qualification.

families.title: Integer division profiles
families.semantic_boundary: BL quot/rem truncate toward zero and rem follows dividend; BL mod follows divisor sign; SMT mod is nonnegative. Represent divisor zero as a language outcome, not an unconstrained total function.

implementation.claim: Implementation must be linked separately; a module or method name is not qualification.

families.title: Exact rationals and mathematical Reals
families.semantic_boundary: Exact mathematical Real is a specification sort, not an alias for native BL integer division or float operations. Preserve rational and algebraic model distinctions.

families.title: Decimal values and quantization
families.semantic_boundary: Current decimal representation stores unbounded digits and scale. Review numeric value versus quantized representation as separate types; symbolic unbounded scales can introduce exponentiation and undecidable fragments.

families.title: Native finite binary64 and IEEE values
families.semantic_boundary: BEAM floats reject NaN and infinity with badarith. IEEE NaN, infinities, signed zero, rounding, bit equality, and IEEE numeric equality need explicit operations and outcome handling.

families.title: Fixed-width bit-vectors
families.semantic_boundary: Width and signedness are part of the sort/operation. BL unbounded bit operations require a conversion contract; wraparound is not ordinary Int arithmetic.

implementation.claim: Implementation must be linked separately; a module or method name is not qualification.

families.title: Bytes and bitstring layouts
families.semantic_boundary: Track bit length, byte alignment, endian and signed interpretation. Incomplete matches and invalid UTF-8 are outcomes, not arbitrary values.

implementation.claim: Implementation must be linked separately; a module or method name is not qualification.

families.title: Unicode codepoint strings and regex
families.semantic_boundary: SMT string length/index operations count codepoints. Regex availability does not imply a complete BL regex API or locale-aware text semantics.

implementation.claim: Implementation must be linked separately; a module or method name is not qualification.

families.title: Grapheme-oriented text
families.semantic_boundary: Grapheme boundaries depend on Unicode rules and can change at concatenation boundaries. Distinguish bytes, codepoints and grapheme indices in sorts; qualify the Unicode version or use explicit finite segmentation facts.

families.title: Keywords, symbols and nominal identities
families.semantic_boundary: Qualified names must remain distinct. Open-ended keyword/symbol universes cannot silently become closed enums. No arbitrary BEAM atom interning from model text.

families.semantic_boundary: A declared datatype is a closed constructor universe. Selectors are guarded by discriminants; SMT selectors on the wrong constructor are total but unspecified.

families.title: Tuples and nominal records
families.semantic_boundary: Tuple/vector/record are distinct runtime kinds. Nominal record identity and hidden __struct__ fields need a declared model, not native representation leakage.

families.semantic_boundary: Runtime success, domain bounds, model availability and solver status are independent. Preserve error kind and successful value; do not prove equivalence by dropping exceptional paths.

families.title: Finite lists
families.semantic_boundary: Empty behavior and returned collection kind are explicit. A finite list model does not certify an infinite or effectful lazy stream.

families.title: Finite indexed vectors
families.semantic_boundary: Represent count and active indices. Current assoc appends at count; review replace-only update versus explicit append. Representation capacity is not a BL bounds error.

families.title: Lazy finite-prefix reasoning
families.semantic_boundary: Realization can diverge or perform effects. Prefix bounds, purity, memoization and termination are explicit assumptions; prefix equality is not whole-stream equality.

families.title: Finite maps with presence
families.semantic_boundary: Track presence separately from values and finite extent. Missing, stored nil and explicit default are distinct. Inactive array payloads must not define extensional map equality.

families.title: Finite sets
bl_jobs: Membership, union/intersection, subset and cardinality laws
families.semantic_boundary: A Boolean-array encoding over a finite universe gives bounded cardinality laws. Do not present finite-universe proofs as theorems over all possible BL values.

families.title: Bags and multiplicities
families.semantic_boundary: Counts are nonnegative integers and extents explicit. A multiset forgets order; bag-level mailbox safety does not imply FIFO behavior.

families.title: Equality, comparison and identity
families.semantic_boundary: Typed SMT equality is congruent representational equality. BL family equivalence can identify different runtime kinds; numeric, representation and observational equivalence need separate scopes. Current Decimal exception may break transitivity through a float.

families.title: Uninterpreted sorts and functions

families.title: First-order quantified laws
families.semantic_boundary: Binders are unique lexical identities. Refuse escaped bound nodes. Triggers and quantified completeness are separate capabilities; do not invent default witnesses.

families.semantic_boundary: Unfolding fuel is a bound, termination a distinct property, and induction requires a sound rule. Higher-order functions need explicit closure/finite-function encodings.

semantic_reviews.title: Strict indexing, defaulting lookup and explicit append
semantic_reviews.observed: Current vector nth returns nil for negative, noninteger or out-of-range indices. get returns its default. assoc replaces, appends exactly at count, and raises beyond count.
semantic_reviews.intended_law: Successful indexed update preserves vector length; strict indexing cannot silently turn a missing element into a nil payload.

alternatives.behavior: Keep permissive nth and append-at-count assoc; encode every branch exactly.
Make nth strict and assoc replace-only; use get/default for absence and conj for append.
Expose explicit at/lookup/update/append operations, then choose aliases separately.

recommendation.rationale: Separate absence from a programming error and replacement from shape change. Prefer strict nth and replace-only assoc as future default aliases after reviewing uses.

integration_consequences: Revisit vector construction/update callers that rely on append-at-count.
Model strict operations with named bounds errors.
Keep representation-capacity :within separate from runtime :defined.

semantic_reviews.title: Absence is a result, nil is a value
semantic_reviews.observed: Current get/get-in default arities distinguish absent paths from present nil, but the default-nil arity intentionally collapses the observation. contains? recovers membership.
semantic_reviews.intended_law: Storing nil must not erase membership; lookup should support distinguishing missing without inventing a sentinel in user code.

alternatives.behavior: Keep nil-punning get and sentinel/default idioms.
Make primary lookup return Option(Value), with Some(nil) distinct from None.
Add lookup/find returning Option and retain get as explicit defaulting convenience.

recommendation.rationale: Option lookup gives formal and ordinary code a faithful absence value while a small defaulting convenience remains useful. Decide the public names before the API hardens.

integration_consequences: Map lowering needs a presence set plus values, or an array of Option.
Model decoding must preserve None, Some(nil), unavailable and default separately.
Query/pull/JSON-facing convenience APIs need explicit absence policy.

semantic_reviews.title: Value equivalence, numeric equality and representation identity
semantic_reviews.observed: Current generic equality groups lists/vectors/lazy finite sequences and ignores metadata. Two Decimals are special-cased by scale-aware representation; other numeric pairs use exact rational comparison. Source therefore suggests a transitivity defect through an exactly representable float.
semantic_reviews.intended_law: Each equality relation must be reflexive/symmetric/transitive on its declared domain; hash and index identity must respect the chosen relation. Substitutivity is scoped to operations that respect that equivalence.

alternatives.behavior: Preserve existing family equivalence and Decimal exception, but expose its exact behavior.
Make default equality kind/representation-sensitive; provide numeric= and sequential-equiv? explicitly.
Use a coherent value-equivalence relation and a separate representation relation; remove the Decimal mixed-policy exception.

recommendation.rationale: First qualify the suspected transitivity defect. Prefer one coherent value equivalence plus explicitly named numeric and representation views. Typed t/eq remains SMT identity; BL equivalence is a profile predicate, never blindly substituted for t/eq.

integration_consequences: Audit map/set hashing, sorted indexes, uniqueness/upsert/retract and Datom codecs as one change.
Cross-kind equality does not imply conj/type predicates are interchangeable.
Do not key cache identity by source display strings or hashes alone.

semantic_reviews.title: A decimal number and a quantized amount can be different types
semantic_reviews.observed: Decimal scale is observable information; exact decimal division can refuse a nonterminating quotient, and rounding has no ambient context.
semantic_reviews.intended_law: Numeric equality should be coherent, and scale-sensitive financial intent should remain expressible and explicit.

alternatives.behavior: One scale-aware Decimal type; all equality/coercion rules must then consistently honor representation.
Normalize Decimal to a numeric value and make scale presentation metadata.
Separate normalized Decimal value from Quantized(amount, scale, rounding-policy) representation.

recommendation.rationale: Separate mathematical value from quantization intent so money contracts can retain cents without making generic equality nontransitive.

integration_consequences: Define literal M meaning and migrations before changing normalization.
Keep exact division and rounded division visibly distinct.
Check hash/index canonicalization and lossless payload codecs independently.

semantic_reviews.title: Mathematical specifications and finite machine floats are separate domains
semantic_reviews.observed: Current solver sort inference maps :float to Real, while runtime numeric arithmetic delegates int/float operations to BEAM. BEAM operations producing NaN or infinities raise badarith.
semantic_reviews.intended_law: A proof about machine arithmetic must preserve rounding, finite-result restrictions and raisedness; a mathematical Real specification must be labelled as mathematical.

alternatives.behavior: Retain Real abstraction, explicitly label it abstract and require a refinement argument for machine claims.
Use finite binary64 semantics by default for native float functions.
Expose Real, raw IEEE and BL finite-float Outcome profiles separately.

recommendation.rationale: Default source-native verification to the runtime profile; use Real only when requested for mathematical specification or a justified abstraction.

integration_consequences: FP sort/rounding constraints and error outcomes must flow through ANF lowering.
Cache identity includes the numeric profile.
Mixed Int/Float/Decimal coercion needs a reviewed, testable contract.

semantic_reviews.title: Name truncating, flooring and Euclidean division explicitly
semantic_reviews.observed: BL quot/rem truncate toward zero and rem follows the dividend. BL mod follows the divisor sign. SMT mod is nonnegative; these disagree for negative divisors.
semantic_reviews.intended_law: Every quotient/remainder pair must satisfy a=b*q+r with its documented sign/range rule; names must identify the selected rule.

alternatives.behavior: Keep names and encode sign corrections in each backend-independent profile.
Choose one division family as the only generic integer division surface.
Expose trunc-div/rem, floor-div/mod and Euclidean-div/mod explicitly; decide short aliases separately.

recommendation.rationale: All three conventions have legitimate uses. Explicit families prevent a solver primitive from silently changing a BL operation.

integration_consequences: Audit the existing direct mod mapping for negative divisors.
Keep division-by-zero as an outcome.
Use a full four-sign canary matrix and algebraic laws, not only positive examples.

semantic_reviews.title: Bytes, codepoints and graphemes deserve named indices
semantic_reviews.observed: BL string count/sequence/subs operations are grapheme-oriented; the SMT string profile is codepoint-oriented. UTF-8 byte length is another quantity.
semantic_reviews.intended_law: An index and length carry the same text unit as the operation consuming them. Conversion is explicit and depends on a declared Unicode profile.

alternatives.behavior: Keep grapheme defaults and refuse SMT lowering unless equivalence is established.
Use codepoints as a simpler core sequence, with grapheme UI functions explicit.
Expose bytes/codepoints/graphemes views with distinct indexed types and conversion operations.

recommendation.rationale: Use codepoint strings for directly supported symbolic theory and retain a named grapheme view for user-facing text; choose ergonomic aliases after reviewing editing APIs.

integration_consequences: Do not lower BL count to str.len by name alone.
Pin Unicode segmentation version or supply finite segmentation evidence.
Grapheme count is not generally additive across concatenation.

semantic_reviews.title: Boolean logic and conditional coercion are separate operations
semantic_reviews.observed: Only nil and false are falsey. Zero, empty string and empty collections are truthy. and/or return selected operands rather than necessarily Bool.
semantic_reviews.intended_law: Logical connectives on Bool obey Boolean laws; conditional coercion must not silently identify an arbitrary value with true or false.

alternatives.behavior: Keep broad truthiness in all source conditionals.
Require Bool in conditions; add explicit boolean coercion.
Keep ordinary truthiness as a language feature, but require Bool terms in formal logic and lower truthiness explicitly in source verification.

recommendation.rationale: Bool-only term construction prevents symbolic coercion bugs without forcing a language-wide conditional change before reviewing usage.

integration_consequences: ANF already records branch structure and operand-return semantics; preserve both.
Review convenience guards that use non-Boolean values intentionally.
Unknown Any-valued predicates need a truthiness term or explicit unsupported result.

semantic_reviews.title: Portable value identity and live resource authority differ
semantic_reviews.observed: Current semantic keys ignore metadata and collapse equal sequential representations, while runtime leases bind exact owners and generations. Records retain nominal kind.
semantic_reviews.intended_law: Portable term identity is content/semantics based; native handle identity is owner/generation based; neither grants runtime authority.

alternatives.behavior: Continue implicit identity conventions at each boundary.
Make all equality representation-sensitive, including storage and metadata.
Declare semantic value keys, lossless representation keys and runtime resource references as distinct types.

recommendation.rationale: This permits portable DAG caching while preserving lossless payloads and strict native lifetime checks. Opaque live resources remain observations.

integration_consequences: Native DAG IDs are never placed inside portable terms.
Cache keys include profile, bounds, backend artifact and query mode.
A stale-generation handle is refused even when its integer ID is reused.

layers: canonical ANF and exact binding identity
native Z3 adapter or native OxiZ adapter
invariants: No SMT-LIB source on the new path.
Source origin is not semantic term identity.
Runtime definedness is independent of finite representation bounds.
Unsupported and unknown never become proved/refuted.
No proof result grants runtime authority.
Semantic redesign is explicitly proposed and never silently installed in the runtime.
